title: const and constexpr: immutable values and pointers

spans.text: `const` prevents later changes; `constexpr` makes a value available at compile time when possible. With `const int* p`, the pointer may change but the value cannot be changed through `p`. With `int* const p`, the pointer address is fixed but the pointed-to value may change. Using `const` on both sides protects both.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Check which side of `*` has `const`. A pointer must not outlive its target, and never write through a pointer to a constant value.
